hint.en: Distinguish terms from partial sums and examine geometric sums, telescoping, and the zero-term condition.

ko: 교대급수에서는 양의 크기 \(b_n\)가 결국 감소하고 0으로 가는지 확인한다. 절댓값 급수도 수렴하면 절대수렴, 절댓값 급수는 발산하지만 원래 급수는 수렴하면 조건수렴이다. 교대급수 오차 \(|R_N|\le b_{N+1}\)는 이 감소·극한 조건이 성립할 때 사용할 수 있다.
en: For an alternating series, check that positive magnitudes \(b_n\) eventually decrease to zero. Convergence of the absolute-value series means absolute convergence; convergence only of the original means conditional convergence. The bound \(|R_N|\le b_{N+1}\) requires the alternating-test conditions.

answer.ko: \(\text{decreasing magnitudes tending to zero imply convergence and }|R_N|\le b_{N+1}\)

Take unused positive terms in their original order until first crossing above the target, then unused negative terms until first crossing below it. Divergence of each signed subseries makes every stage finite. Each overshoot is bounded by the magnitude of the last term of its block, hence tends to zero. Intermediate sums lie between the adjacent crossing values, so all partial sums approach the target. Both ordered sign lists are consumed indefinitely, using every nonzero term once; insert zero terms between blocks.
